# PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER] This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER] Contents of this practice direction

## 1. Scope and interpretation

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 1. Scope and interpretation] 1.1 This Practice Direction specifies the jurisdiction that may be exercised by a legal adviser and any restrictions that apply relating to—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 1. Scope and interpretation] (a) claims proceeding in the Civil National Business Centre; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 1. Scope and interpretation] (b) applications which are required by a rule or practice direction to be made at that Centre.

## 1.2 In this Practice Direction—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 1.2 In this Practice Direction—] (a) “the Civil National Business Centre” includes the Production Centre and Money Claim Online;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 1.2 In this Practice Direction—] (b) “legal adviser” means a court officer assigned to the County Court who is—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 1.2 In this Practice Direction—] (i) a barrister;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 1.2 In this Practice Direction—] (ii) a solicitor; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 1.2 In this Practice Direction—] (iii) a Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Legal Executives, or a CILEX lawyer,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 1.2 In this Practice Direction—] who may exercise the jurisdiction of the County Court with regard to the matters set out in paragraph 2.1 and in the schedule to this Practice Direction, with the consent of the relevant Designated Civil Judge or their nominee.

## 2. Jurisdiction of the County Court that may be exercised by a legal adviser

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 2. Jurisdiction of the County Court that may be exercised by a legal adviser] 2.1 A legal adviser may exercise the jurisdiction of the County Court with regard to the matters set out in the first column of the Schedule to this Practice Direction, subject to the corresponding restrictions in the second column.

## 3. Reconsideration of a decision made by a legal adviser

## 3.1 Decisions of a legal adviser will be made without a hearing.

## 3.2 A party may request any decision of a legal adviser to be reconsidered by a District Judge.

## 3.3 A request must be filed within 14 days after the party is served with notice of the decision.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 3.3 A request must be filed within 14 days after the party is served with notice of the decision.] 3.4 The request may include a summary of the issue and an explanation of why the reconsideration is sought.

## 3.5 Reconsideration will take place without a hearing.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 3.5 Reconsideration will take place without a hearing.] Schedule – Jurisdiction of the County Court that may be exercised by a legal adviser

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 3.5 Reconsideration will take place without a hearing.] Work type

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 3.5 Reconsideration will take place without a hearing.] Restrictions on the exercise of jurisdiction and modifications of the Civil Procedure Rules

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 3.5 Reconsideration will take place without a hearing.] Limited to errors made by the court.

## 2.  Application to extend time for service of the claim form pursuant to rule 7.6

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 2.  Application to extend time for service of the claim form pursuant to rule 7.6] Limited to the first such application and further limited to applications—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 2.  Application to extend time for service of the claim form pursuant to rule 7.6] (a) made within the period specified in rule 7.6(2); and (b) where the limitation period for bringing the claim has not expired.

## 3.  Application for an order permitting service at an alternative place, pursuant to rule 6.15(1)

## 4.  Applications for an extension of time in which to serve the particulars of claim

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 4.  Applications for an extension of time in which to serve the particulars of claim] Limited to applications made within the period specified in rule 7.4 or any extension of that time for service of the particulars of claim.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 4.  Applications for an extension of time in which to serve the particulars of claim] 5.  Applications to amend a claimant’s or defendant’s address or details after service, pursuant to rule 17.1(2)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 4.  Applications for an extension of time in which to serve the particulars of claim] 6.  Application to amend the particulars of claim or the amount of the claim pursuant to rule 17.1(2), but excluding any application to which rule 17.4(1)(b) applies

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 4.  Applications for an extension of time in which to serve the particulars of claim] Limited to—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 4.  Applications for an extension of time in which to serve the particulars of claim] (a) applications received before a defence is filed; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 4.  Applications for an extension of time in which to serve the particulars of claim] (b) if an application is received after a defence is filed, claims which have been, or would normally be, allocated to the small claims track or to the fast track.

## 7.  Application to add or substitute a party to the proceedings pursuant to rule 19.4

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 7.  Application to add or substitute a party to the proceedings pursuant to rule 19.4] Limited to applications where all existing parties, upon whom

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 7.  Application to add or substitute a party to the proceedings pursuant to rule 19.4] the claim has been served and who have acknowledged service, and the proposed new party agree to the addition or substitution.

## 8.  Application or request to set aside default judgment, pursuant to rule 13.2

## 9.   Application to set aside default judgment, pursuant to rule 13.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 9.   Application to set aside default judgment, pursuant to rule 13.3] Limited to applications where—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 9.   Application to set aside default judgment, pursuant to rule 13.3] (a) all parties consent; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 9.   Application to set aside default judgment, pursuant to rule 13.3] (b) the judgment is not satisfied.

## 10.  Application to vary default judgment entered under Part 12, pursuant to rule 13.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 10.  Application to vary default judgment entered under Part 12, pursuant to rule 13.3] Limited to applications which relate to the time and/or rate of payment.

## 11.  Application to extend time for filing or serving a defence

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 11.  Application to extend time for filing or serving a defence] Limited to the first such application by each defendant and subject to the further limitation that time can be extended for a period not exceeding 28 days.

## 12.  Application to make a counterclaim after a defence has been filed, pursuant to rule 20.4(2)(b)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 12.  Application to make a counterclaim after a defence has been filed, pursuant to rule 20.4(2)(b)] Limited to applications where the limitation period for bringing the counterclaim has not expired.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 12.  Application to make a counterclaim after a defence has been filed, pursuant to rule 20.4(2)(b)] 13.  Application to appoint a new litigation friend in substitution for an existing one pursuant to rule 21.7(1)(c)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 12.  Application to make a counterclaim after a defence has been filed, pursuant to rule 20.4(2)(b)] 14.  Application to extend time for complying with a notice of proposed allocation in accordance with rule 26.4(1)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 12.  Application to make a counterclaim after a defence has been filed, pursuant to rule 20.4(2)(b)] Provided that any extension is for a period not exceeding 28 days.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 12.  Application to make a counterclaim after a defence has been filed, pursuant to rule 20.4(2)(b)] 15.  Application to stay proceedings pursuant to rule 26.5(3) or to extend the period of a stay pursuant to rule 26.5(4)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 12.  Application to make a counterclaim after a defence has been filed, pursuant to rule 20.4(2)(b)] Provided that any stay, or extension of the stay, is for a period not exceeding 28 days.

## 16.  Application to remove a stay of proceedings

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 16.  Application to remove a stay of proceedings] Limited to applications where —

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 16.  Application to remove a stay of proceedings] (a) all parties consent; or (b) the order staying the proceedings was made by a legal adviser

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 16.  Application to remove a stay of proceedings] Limited to applications where all parties consent to the payment.”.

## 18.  Entering and sealing an agreed judgment pursuant to rule 40.6(2)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 18.  Entering and sealing an agreed judgment pursuant to rule 40.6(2)] 19.  Applications for judgments or orders (including orders made under rule 40.6(3)(b)(ii)) in terms agreed pursuant to rule 40.6(5)

## 20.  Application for an Order that a solicitor has ceased to act pursuant to rule 42.3

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 20.  Application for an Order that a solicitor has ceased to act pursuant to rule 42.3] 21. Applications for a certificate of judgment by a judgment creditor who seeks to enforce a County Court judgment abroad, pursuant to rule 74.12

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 2E – JURISDICTION OF THE COUNTY COURT THAT MAY BE EXERCISED BY A LEGAL ADVISER > 20.  Application for an Order that a solicitor has ceased to act pursuant to rule 42.3] 22. Applications for a certificate of money provisions by a judgment creditor who seeks to enforce a money judgment of the County Court in another part of the United Kingdom, pursuant to rule 74.17
